results.note: Connected: npm start now preloads argus/agent with ARGUS_OUTPUT=.argus/raw.ndjson (start:plain keeps the original) and argus:collect runs tools copied into .argus/tools. The dashboard SSE capture summarized in tool-result.json had 28 windows and 6 incoming GET / spans; a restart from the saved recipe showed 29 windows and 6 spans. ps was sandbox-blocked, so cleanup was confirmed by session exits and closed ports.

GET /work p50 10 ms, p99/max 400 ms at 2000-4000 ms; event loop max 100 ms, sample p99 50 ms, GC 12 ms total, backpressure 18 ms at /app/stream.js:12:3, flat memory. Ranked untraced application or dependency waiting first, without naming a function or dependency; proposed a paired capture with handler sub-timers.
compare returned comparable=false. Named the 100 vs 60 request mismatch and the 3000 ms declared vs 6000 ms recorded duration; all deltas zero; declared no improvement.

heapUsed/heapTotal flat at 1/4 MiB while RSS rose 20 to 70 MiB, matched by external (2 to 52 MiB) and arrayBuffers (1 to 51 MiB). Called it external/ArrayBuffer pressure, not a proven leak; no snapshot; proposed repeated cycles with post-GC idle.

eventLoop.max > 50,000,000 ns for 2 windows; the exact 50 ms window does not count. Fired at 3000-4000 (70 ms), resolved at 4000-5000; normal replay had no alerts. Activation recipe says to add sinks for delivery.
Empty recording: no measurements, hypotheses or root cause; loss unknown; gave a capture recipe for spans and runtime samples.

Captured 500 ms of real dashboard SSE (6 history events, 0 live). Kept loss unknown and reported backpressure call sites and external/arrayBuffers memory as unavailable from windows; no request symptom or cause claimed.
Inconclusive: 100 ms event-loop maximum and 90 ms maximum sample p99; stated that a global p99 cannot be reconstructed from per-sample percentiles.

Ran with every Bash command in the OS sandbox. Connected with app-owned scripts (start:argus and argus:collect over .argus/start-app.sh, .argus/collect.sh and tools copied to .argus/tools); the original start is unchanged. .argus/verify.sh starts the app and collector, sends requests, captures the dashboard SSE and stops both in one command. Two runs from the saved recipe each showed 7 windows and 8 incoming spans; raw.ndjson had 17 samples. Only the one-off copy command referred to the plugin; the recipe defaults NODE to the verified Node binary, overridable.

Same measurements with units; noted the event-loop, GC and backpressure samples are identical in fast and slow periods, so none tracks the 400 ms step. Hypotheses only, with a finer-interval capture plus handler timing or --cpu-prof as the distinguishing experiment. Minor: one limitation loosely calls a sample p99 a maximum of sub-samples.
compare returned comparable=false. Named the request-count and duration mismatches; all deltas zero; declared the comparison inconclusive, not an improvement or a null effect.

Separated flat heap from external/arrayBuffers growth that matches RSS; no post-GC baseline or repeated cycle, so a leak is not established; proposed repeated start/stop cycles comparing post-drain baselines; no snapshot.

Strict > 50,000,000 ns for 2 windows; the 50 ms window is not a breach (>= would fire a window earlier). Fired at 3000-4000, resolved at 4000-5000; normal replay silent; activation with a file sink and a note that alerts without a sink stay in the ring and dashboard.
Empty file: insufficient evidence, zeros mean no data rather than health, no root cause; gave a capture command and the evidence needed.

Real dashboard SSE, 6 history events and 0 live; loss unknown; hotspots and external/arrayBuffers memory unavailable from windows; maxSampleP99Ns described as a maximum of per-sample p99s, not a global p99.
Inconclusive: 100 ms event-loop maximum and 90 ms maximum sample p99 (t=1000); refused to treat it as a global p99.
